obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security: unauthorized access of electronic data containing personal information of Florida residents (owner-operator Social Security numbers, driver license numbers, or driver location, each with a name). The clock runs from determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination. Up to 15 more days only if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days; delay also allowed on a written law enforcement request
notify: Each affected Florida individual, by mail or email to the address on file
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - plan to the 30-day clock

obligation: Florida no-harm determination
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the owner reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Determination in writing, kept at least 5 years; provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - only if the determination is made

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - about 350 carriers and drivers in all, most outside Florida; recount at every incident

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: No - fewer than 1,000 individuals on file

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the business (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the business (TMS, email and file suite, accounting, tracking app) has a breach of a system it maintains
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days following its determination of the breach
notify: The business (owner); the business then gives the notices above
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - confirm in each vendor's terms (POAM-003)

obligation: Other states' breach laws
trigger: Affected carriers or drivers who reside outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - most carriers and drivers live outside Florida; counsel applies the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: Largest shipper incident notice
citation: Master broker-shipper agreement (2025), incident notice clause
trigger: Security incident affecting the shipper's data (rates, tenders, shipment details)
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the shortest clock in this matrix; contract term, not a regulation

obligation: Railroad portal credential notice
citation: Railroad customer portal terms of use
trigger: Suspected unauthorized use of a portal user ID (for example, credentials saved in the infected laptop's browser)
deadline: Promptly, per the portal terms
notify: Each railroad's portal administrator or customer service center; the affected shipper
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract term

obligation: Respond to a surety claim notice
trigger: Carriers left unpaid during the incident claim against the $75,000 surety bond and the surety notifies the broker
deadline: Within 7 business days, or the surety may pay a claim it finds valid; a payment below $75,000 starts suspension
notify: Surety company (written response on the validity of the claim)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - answer every claim; attorney is the backup responder (POL-01 11.3)

obligation: Respond to an FMCSA suspension notice
trigger: FMCSA serves notice after a surety or financial institution report
deadline: Within 7 business days of service, show the notice was in error, the bond was restored, or the claims were satisfied; otherwise authority is suspended
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if a claim payment occurs

obligation: Correct the FMCSA registration record
trigger: The attacker changed contact details on the FMCSA record, or the owner changes the business email or phone during recovery
deadline: Within 30 days after the change
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons

obligation: Voluntary law enforcement and CISA report
citation: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center; CISA incident reporting
trigger: Ransomware, data theft, or a diverted payment
deadline: As soon as practical; same day for a diverted payment, to improve the chance of recovery through the bank
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary - recommended

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy terms
applies_at_this_tier: No standalone cyber or social engineering fraud policy; ask the insurance agent whether the general liability policy has a data breach endorsement

obligation: TSA SD cybersecurity incident reporting (rail, passenger rail/transit, pipeline)
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a covered owner/operator
deadline: Within 24 hours of identification
applies_at_this_tier: No - a broker is not a railroad in 49 CFR 1580.101 and has not been designated by TSA (P03 G-001, G-002)

obligation: TSA significant security concern report
trigger: Significant security concern at a person covered by part 1580
deadline: Within 24 hours of initial discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - a broker is not among the persons in 49 CFR 1580.1(a) (P03 G-003)

obligation: Report actual or threatened cyber incident involving vessel, harbor, port or waterfront facility
citation: 33 CFR 6.16-1 (as amended by E.O. 14116); 33 CFR 101.620(b)(7) (reportable cyber incidents to National Response Center)
trigger: Cyber incident involving a vessel, harbor, port, or waterfront facility
deadline: Immediately
notify: FBI, CISA and the Captain of the Port; National Response Center (1-800-424-8802) for reportable cyber incidents if not already reported under 6.16-1
applies_at_this_tier: No - no vessel, port, or waterfront facility

obligation: Aviation significant cybersecurity incident reporting
trigger: Incident at a TSA-regulated airport or aircraft operator
deadline: Per security program (SSI)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business arranges no air transportation

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident / ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment) - not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published; as proposed, the business is SBA-small and not in the transportation criteria of proposed 226.2(b)(14) (P03 section 5)

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Covered equipment found while performing a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
trigger: Covered article found while performing a federal contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
